clue.text: It may be readily edited to contain trivial reading matter

definitions.text: It may be readily edited to contain trivial reading matter

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
text that has been edited is reworked, so the letters of readily are rearranged

parts.note: pap is soft, worthless reading material

explanation.surface: A remark that some newspaper is easily trimmed down so it can carry lightweight content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges the letters into DAILYER. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a tabloid full of fluff, its text cut and polished by editors.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper printed each weekday is put together by editors and often filled with light gossip and froth.

clue.text: An amusing situation repeatedly found in popular British novels

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece made from the first words appears twice in a row

parts.note: a gas is informal for something great fun, a hoot

explanation.surface: Comedy keeps cropping up in well-loved British fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA SAGA is a British genre of middle-class rural family novels, named after the Aga, a large cast-iron kitchen range.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a genre of bestselling domestic fiction set in comfortable English country households.

clue.text: Urgent request, no parking in this pastoral setting

indicators.note: no parking says that the letter for parking is to be dropped from the word

parts.note: a plea is an earnest, pressing appeal
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A desperate appeal about a no-parking rule in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a meadow or grassy field, the stuff of rural poetry.

clue.text: A nut's what might be said to be under the bed

indicators.note: what might be said points to a word spoken, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a chamber pot kept beneath the bed could jokingly be called a pee can

explanation.surface: A riddle claiming that a certain nut's name describes something kept beneath the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A chamber pot, once kept under the bed for use at night, could be called a 'pee can', a phrase pronounced like the nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is the nut of a North American hickory tree, used in pies.

clue.text: Heartless deal breaking fruit sellers

indicators.note: breaking means the fruit word is split open to admit the other piece

parts.note: pears are a fruit

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word deal is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A ruthless trader smashing up a fruit stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit sellers' reads as one phrase, like grocers, but 'fruit' belongs to the wordplay and only 'sellers' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedlars are hawkers who travel about offering small goods for sale.

clue.text: Doctor who's after run of publicity from these?

definitions.text: Doctor who's after run of publicity from these?

indicators.note: after places the rearranged piece behind the run of letters before it

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
o' is a shortened form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp
ads are advertisements, publicity

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of who's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a famous TV time-traveller tours the country hoping to drum up attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges the letters into HOWS. 'Doctor who' suggests the TV time-traveller. The whole clue is the definition: touring shows bring publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Touring presentations travel from town to town to promote a product, a broadcaster or a cause.

clue.text: What's behind bar? Tango

parts.note: bar in the sense of except, as is but
T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Asking what lies beyond a pub counter, with a dance thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it means 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is the buttocks, informally, the part of the body behind a person.

clue.text: What has fruit and nuts with it, covering plate?

indicators.note: covering means the joined words close round the plate piece

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, nuts
taken as written
PL is the abbreviation for plate

explanation.surface: Asking which dish comes with fruit and nuts, served over a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit and nuts' looks like one list of ingredients, but 'nuts' is the slang word for crazy and belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert is a halved banana with ice cream and toppings, so it always comes with something sweet from a tree.

clue.text: Chicken pieces smelling bad in vans of Tesco and sainsbury

indicators.note: in puts the smelly word between those two letters
vans are the fronts, as in vanguard, so the first letters of the two shop names are taken

parts.note: high describes meat or game that has started to go off

explanation.surface: Rotten poultry found in supermarket delivery vans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vans' looks like delivery lorries, but it means fronts, giving T and S. Tesco and Sainsbury's are big British supermarket chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Thighs are a common cut of chicken sold in packs.

clue.text: Even British airways facing cut

parts.note: lanced means cut open, as a boil

explanation.surface: A news line about the national airline facing cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something balanced is level, with equal weight on each side.

clue.text: Haggard tart heads off for her older relative?

indicators.note: heads off means each of the two words loses its first letter

parts.note: gaunt means haggard, drawn and thin
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: A worn-out woman takes a pastry and leaves for a relative's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' takes the G from GAUNT and the P from PIE. 'tart' and 'Haggard' suggest an unkind description of a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie is an affectionate word for a parent's sister, a family member a generation up.

clue.text: Woody entrance to field initially sunken

indicators.note: initially puts that letter at the start, before the name
the entrance to a word is its first letter

parts.note: Woody Allen is the American film director

explanation.surface: A wooded gateway into a field that has sunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woody' looks like an adjective for trees, but it is Woody Allen, the film director.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen means having dropped down or caved in, like a collapsed floor.

clue.text: Up-to-date position from selectors at ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Team selectors at the cricket ground giving news of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a sports ground but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent tally in a match tells you how things stand right now.

clue.text: A bishop's vice — the drink!

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a vice is a sin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman's secret weakness turns out to be alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is both part of the wordplay and attached to 'drink'; only 'drink' defines, with 'the' giving THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green spirit flavoured with wormwood.

clue.text: Shop starting out gets hostile comments at the end of the day?

definitions.text: hostile comments at the end of the day?

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or in disarray, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop opening up attracts nasty remarks at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like 'starting out', a new business, but it rearranges SHOP and STARTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Parting shots are barbed final remarks made as someone leaves.

clue.text: Most slender weapon kept in secluded place

indicators.note: kept in means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a nest is a snug hideaway
an arrow is a weapon

explanation.surface: A very thin weapon is stashed away in a hidden spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowest means having the least width, the thinnest of all.

clue.text: Present in second delivery is a plant

indicators.note: in puts the present word between the letter for second and the delivery word

parts.note: a drop is a delivery, as of goods
now means the present time

explanation.surface: A gift turns up in the second post and it is a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but it means now.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdrops are small white flowers that bloom in late winter.

clue.text: Fools train having drunk gallons, left to drop

indicators.note: having means holding something inside, so the train word encloses the rest

parts.note: a string is a line or series, like a train of animals

indicators.note: drunk means messed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to drop says that the letter for left goes from the word gallons

explanation.surface: A train guzzling fuel and then shedding a load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' takes one L away, leaving GALONS; 'drunk' rearranges that to GSALON, which sits before the final G of the train word.
explanation.definitionFit: To string someone along is to deceive them, keeping them hoping falsely.

clue.text: Yahoo's that corrupted on a test

indicators.note: corrupted data is garbled, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A search engine whose data was corrupted during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yahoo' looks like the web company, but it is a boor, as in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, uncultured lout, and such a person lacks refinement.

clue.text: Drink to make a bishop lustful

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
randy means lustful

explanation.surface: Alcohol that turns a cleric amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: Ford's blooming strike off

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it
flowers that are out are in bloom

explanation.surface: A Ford car's flowering, or a carmaker's strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like the car maker, but it is the verb for crossing a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross out a name is to delete it with a line, removing it from a list.

clue.text: Being excessively close to Washington restricts a north American city

indicators.note: restricts means the two joined pieces hem in the letter a

parts.note: OTT is over the top, excessive
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: Something too near to the US capital restricting a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' looks like the US capital, but it is WA, the state. OTTAWA is the capital of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the Canadian capital, in Ontario.

clue.text: Individual cases I caught being delayed

indicators.note: cases means the word for individual wraps round the other letters

parts.note: one means a single individual
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Separate court cases, one where I was caught, are being held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like lawsuits, but it means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put on ice is shelved or postponed for later.

clue.text: Home alone? Boots may be holding it

parts.note: in means at home
sole means alone, only

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is home by themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a British chain of chemists that sells shoe inserts; boots for the feet also hold them.
explanation.definitionFit: An inner sole sits inside footwear for comfort.

clue.text: Acne risk is reduced with this

definitions.text: Acne risk is reduced with this

indicators.note: reduced in the sense of broken down to pieces, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A promise that a routine will lower your chances of spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' rearranges the letters. The whole clue is the definition: looking after your complexion cuts down on spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansing and moisturising the face helps keep pimples at bay.

clue.text: Pieces of haddock served up, not this!

definitions.text: Pieces of haddock served up, not this!

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
pieces of means a run of letters is taken from inside the word haddock

explanation.surface: A fish order that turns out to be the wrong fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces of' takes DOC from inside 'haddock', and 'served up' turns it round. The whole clue is the definition: the fish served is not haddock.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod is a white fish often served instead of, and confused with, its cousin.

clue.text: Courier for example, is kind

explanation.surface: A messenger is described as kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courier' looks like a messenger, but it is the typewriter font.
explanation.definitionFit: Courier is a typeface, a style of printed lettering; type also means a sort or category.

clue.text: Subject of talk: northern hollows and heights

parts.note: a theme is the topic of a speech
dips are hollows in the ground

explanation.surface: A lecture on the northern landscape of valleys and hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendips are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: These hills rise above the Somerset Levels, a range of upland.
